root_cause.text: In the virtio_bt driver, the RX work function (virtbt_rx_work) called skb_put with a device-reported length without validating it against the actual buffer size delivered to virtio, allowing a malicious backend to trigger out-of-bounds memory access via an oversized length or read uninitialized data via a zero length.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "virtbt_rx_work() calls skb_put(skb, len) where len comes directly from virtqueue_get_buf() with no validation against the buffer we posted to the device" and notes that checking skb_tailroom was insufficient because alloc_skb may leave more room than the 1000 bytes actually handed to the device. The patch defines VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE (1000) and gates on "!len || len > VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE" to reject invalid lengths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Define a constant for virtual Bluetooth receive buffer size to improve code clarity and maintainability.
intent_record.what: Added a new preprocessor macro definition `VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE` with value 1000, placed after the version string definition and before the enum.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant that can be used for receive buffer sizing in the virtual Bluetooth driver, enabling consistent buffer allocation and easy adjustment.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace magic number 1000 with named macro VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE to improve code readability and maintainability.
intent_record.what: Replaced hardcoded literal 1000 with macro VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE in alloc_skb and sg_init_one calls.
intent_record.how: Behavior is unchanged; the macro expands to the same value (presumably 1000). The code now uses a symbolic constant instead of a magic number.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds check for received packet length to prevent memory corruption from invalid lengths.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check for len being zero or exceeding VIRTBT_RX_BUF_SIZE before proceeding with skb_put and virtbt_rx_handle; if invalid, log error and free skb.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential memory corruption or crashes by ensuring that skb_put is only called with a valid length; invalid lengths cause the skb to be freed and an error message to be logged.
